ev.benz-1886.t: Karl Benz builds the first petrol motor car in 1886 and sells the first commercial automobile.
ev.russian-flu-1889.t: The first reports came from Bukhara in May 1889, probably of malaria; the flu itself seems to have appeared in Tomsk province in western Siberia in October. St Petersburg and Berlin had it by November, Paris and London in December, and the United States reported its first case on 18 December. By May 1890 it had reached India, Singapore, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and China, and it returned in waves until 1895.
ev.polio-epidemics.t: The first recognised American epidemic struck Vermont in 1894, with 132 cases. New York lost more than 2,000 people in 1916, and 1952 brought the worst American epidemic and an outbreak in Copenhagen that led Bjørn Ibsen to positive-pressure ventilation. Salk’s vaccine was announced on 12 April 1955 and Sabin’s oral vaccine licensed in 1962; wild poliovirus now survives only in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
ev.radio-1895.t: Guglielmo Marconi sends his first radio signals in 1895; in the 1920s radio becomes the entertainment of the world.
ev.spanish-american-1898.t: Cuba rises against Spain in 1895; the Spanish–American War of 1898 ends Spanish rule in Cuba. In the Philippines the revolution of 1896–1898 ends in a Filipino victory.
ev.xrays-1895.t: Wilhelm Röntgen identifies X-rays in 1895 and Henri Becquerel discovers radioactivity in 1896.
ev.adwa-1896.t: Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa in 1896, twelve years after the Berlin Conference divided Africa among the European powers.
ev.boxer-1899.t: The Boxer Rebellion in northern China is suppressed by the Eight-Nation Alliance in 1900–1901.
ev.wright-1903.t: The Wright brothers make the first controlled heavier-than-air flight on 17 December 1903.
ev.russo-japanese-war.t: Japan attacks Port Arthur on 8 February 1904 and destroys the Baltic Fleet at Tsushima; the war ends in Japanese victory in September 1905.
ev.tsushima-1905.t: Russia’s Baltic squadron under Rozhestvensky sails for about seven months to relieve Port Arthur and arrives too late. In May 1905 the Japanese fleet destroys it in the Tsushima strait, the most crushing defeat in the history of the Russian navy; the flagship Knyaz Suvorov is sunk.
ev.revolution-1905.t: Troops fire on marchers approaching the Winter Palace on 22 January 1905; strikes force the October Manifesto.
ev.great-migration-us.t: About six million Black Americans left the South between 1910 and 1970: about 1.6 million in the first wave to 1940, mostly from rural areas to northern industrial cities, and at least five million in the second wave to 1970, to the North and the West. Almost half of Mississippi’s first-wave migrants ended in Chicago.
ev.qing-falls-1912.t: The Qing dynasty ends in 1912 and a republic follows in China.
ev.titanic-1912.t: RMS Titanic strikes an iceberg in the North Atlantic in April 1912 and sinks with an estimated 2,224 people aboard.
ev.sarajevo-1914.t: Gavrilo Princip shoots Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914.
ev.western-front.t: Trench lines run from the Channel to Switzerland after the Marne in September 1914; Verdun and the Somme in 1916 cost hundreds of thousands of lives; the armistice is signed on 11 November 1918.
ev.marne-1914.n: The First Battle of the Marne
ev.marne-1914.t: Germany’s advance on Paris is halted on the Marne in September 1914. The quick victory fails, the war becomes a war on two fronts and the Western Front settles into trenches.
ev.armenian-genocide-1915.t: In 1915–1917 the Ottoman Empire destroys its Armenian people, with Assyrians and Greeks, in deportations and massacres.
ev.gallipoli-1915.t: British, French and ANZAC forces land on the Gallipoli peninsula in 1915; the Ottoman Empire repels them and the campaign is abandoned in 1916.
ev.arab-revolt-1916.t: The Arabs of the Hejaz rise against Ottoman rule in 1916.
ev.somme-1916.t: On 1 July 1916, the first day on the Somme, the British army suffers 57,500 casualties, 19,200 of them dead. By November the battle has cost about 420,000 British, 200,000 French and 500,000 German casualties.
ev.verdun-1916.t: Germany attacks the French positions at Verdun from February to December 1916. The two armies suffer roughly 700,000 to 975,000 casualties, the French more.
ev.russian-revolution-1917.t: The February rising ends the monarchy on 8 March 1917; Lenin returns by train through Germany and Sweden in April; the Bolsheviks take the Winter Palace on 7 November.
ev.russians-after-1917.t: Most White émigrés left in 1917–1920, from southern Russia and Ukraine to Turkey and on to Yugoslavia, Bulgaria, Czechoslovakia and Poland; about 150,000 fled to Istanbul, the flow swelling after the loss of Crimea in 1920. Paris held the largest community, Belgrade the second; Berlin and Prague thrived; about 127,000 Russians lived in Harbin in 1920 and many more in Shanghai.
ev.brest-litovsk-1918.t: Soviet Russia leaves the war at Brest-Litovsk in March 1918.
ev.spanish-flu.t: The conventional first case was at Camp Funston, Kansas, on 4 March 1918, and the spring wave was mild. A far deadlier second wave rose from late August, probably carried by ships from Brest to Freetown and Boston; a third came in the winter of 1919, reaching Australia and Madagascar, and a fourth in 1920 in the United States, Mexico, Peru and Brazil. Spanish newspapers reported the disease from May 1918 while censors elsewhere kept quiet, which gave it its name.
ev.versailles-1919.t: The treaty of 28 June 1919 redraws the borders of Europe.
ev.hiv-aids.t: HIV-1 crossed from chimpanzees in southern Cameroon, and the first suspected human cases may have been in Léopoldville, today Kinshasa, in the 1920s; samples from 1959–60 hold early infections. It reached Haiti about 1966–67, the United States about 1969, New York about 1971 and San Francisco about 1976. On 5 June 1981 the CDC reported unusual pneumonia in five gay men in Los Angeles, the first clinical report of AIDS.
ev.insulin-1921.t: Insulin is developed in the early 1920s and roughly triples the life expectancy of diabetics.
ev.ussr-1922.t: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics is created on 30 December 1922.
ev.greek-turkish-1923.t: Over a million Greek Orthodox subjects had already fled Turkey when Smyrna fell in September 1922. The convention signed at Lausanne on 30 January 1923 made the exchange compulsory and religious: about 1,221,489 Greek Orthodox Christians were displaced from Turkey and 355,000–400,000 Muslims from Greece.
ev.caliphate-1924.t: Mustafa Kemal abolishes the caliphate in 1924, two years after the Soviet Union adopts state atheism.
ev.television-1926.t: John Logie Baird shows the first live working television system in London in 1926, as radio becomes the entertainment of the decade.
ev.penicillin-1928.t: Alexander Fleming rediscovers penicillin on 3 September 1928.
ev.crash-1929.t: The crash of 24–29 October 1929 opens the Great Depression.
ev.holodomor-1932.t: A man-made famine kills millions in Soviet Ukraine in 1932–1933.
ev.hitler-1933.t: Adolf Hitler is appointed chancellor of Germany on 30 January 1933.
ev.long-march-1934.t: The Chinese Red Army breaks out of its southern base in 1934 and marches through the west of China to the north in 1934–1935.
ev.spanish-civil-war.t: The war begins with the coup of July 1936 and ends in Franco's victory in 1939.
ev.kristallnacht-1938.t: In November 1938 the Nazi state unleashes a pogrom against Germany’s Jews.
ev.poland-1939.t: Germany invades Poland on 1 September 1939; Britain and France declare war on 3 September.
ev.barbarossa.t: Germany invades the Soviet Union in June 1941; the campaign runs to December, when the advance halts before Moscow.
ev.pearl-harbor.t: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 and the United States enters the war.
ev.stalingrad.t: The battle begins in August 1942 and ends on 2 February 1943 with the German surrender.
ev.midway-1942.t: Japan’s advance across the Pacific is halted at Midway in June 1942, six months after Pearl Harbor.
ev.reactor-1942.t: Enrico Fermi’s reactor achieves the first controlled nuclear chain reaction in 1942. Three years later the bombs fall on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
ev.kursk-1943.t: Germany attacks at Kursk on 5 July 1943 and calls the offensive off within a week. The Soviet counter-offensive begins on 12 July and ends German superiority in the east.
ev.normandy-1944.t: Allied forces land in Normandy on 6 June 1944 and break out towards Paris.
ev.germans-1945.n: The flight and expulsion of the Germans
ev.germans-1945.t: About seven million Germans from the eastern territories and three million from Czechoslovakia were among roughly 12 million who fled or were expelled between 1944 and 1950, under the Potsdam agreement of August 1945 which recognised the ‘transfer to Germany of German populations’. They were distributed among the four occupation zones, about 1.9 million to the American zone alone.
ev.hiroshima-1945.t: Atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and Nagasaki on 9 August.
ev.un-1945.t: The UN Charter is signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
ev.decolonisation.n: The end of the European empires
ev.decolonisation.t: In the decades after 1945 decolonisation brings independence to most of Africa and Asia. By the end of the century nearly a billion Africans live in the new nation states.
ev.transistor-1947.t: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, under William Shockley at Bell Labs, make the first transistor in 1947. The integrated circuit follows in 1958–1959 and the microprocessor, Intel’s 4004, in 1971.
ev.partition-1947.t: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947 and India on 15 August. About 6.5 million Muslims moved into West Punjab and 4.7 million Hindus and Sikhs into East Punjab, where the transfer was organised because of the violence; Delhi received about 500,000 Hindus and Sikhs and lost about 330,000 Muslims. Bengal divided more slowly and for longer.
ev.palestinians-1948.t: Between 31 December 1947 and 20 July 1949 more than 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled, about 80% of the Arab inhabitants of what became Israel; the UN Conciliation Commission counted 711,000 refugees outside Israel in September 1949, and between 400 and 600 villages were destroyed. The refugees went to Gaza, the hill towns, Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt; 4.9 million people, descendants included, are registered with UNRWA.
ev.prc-1949.t: Mao proclaims the People's Republic from Tiananmen on 1 October 1949.
ev.nato-1949.t: The North Atlantic Treaty is signed on 4 April 1949.
ev.korean-war.t: North Korea invades the South on 25 June 1950.
ev.dna-1953.t: The structure of DNA is determined in 1953, the year of the coronation of Elizabeth II.
ev.dien-bien-phu-1954.t: The French garrison at Dien Bien Phu surrenders in May 1954, losing about a tenth of French Union manpower in Indochina. The Geneva Accords of July end the French war and divide Vietnam at the 17th parallel.
ev.vietnam-war.t: The war between the communist North and the American-backed South grows after the Gulf of Tonkin in 1964; American strength peaks at 543,400 in April 1969, and the Tet offensive of 1968 strikes more than 100 towns. Between 970,000 and 3 million Vietnamese die, with 58,220 Americans.
ev.hungary-1956.t: Hungarians rise against their Soviet-aligned government in 1956, after the Poznań protests in Poland.
ev.treaty-of-rome-1957.t: Six states sign the Treaty of Rome on 25 March 1957, the seed of the European Union.
ev.sputnik-1957.t: Sputnik 1 is launched on 4 October 1957; the space age begins.
ev.asian-flu-1957.t: An epidemic was noted in western Guizhou in late February 1957 and had spread across China by mid-March. Thousands were sick in Hong Kong by April, and Singapore, first to warn the WHO on 4 May, had it from there. India had a million cases by June, when Britain, the Netherlands and the United States were reached.
ev.china-famine-1959.t: The Great Chinese Famine of 1959–1962 kills tens of millions.
ev.pill-1960.t: The oral contraceptive pill comes on the market in 1960. Theodore Maiman makes the first working laser the same year.
ev.gagarin-1961.t: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space on 12 April 1961.
ev.berlin-wall.t: Construction of the Wall begins on 13 August 1961; it falls on 9 November 1989.
ev.cuban-missile-crisis.t: The crisis of 16–29 October 1962 brings the superpowers to the edge of nuclear war.
ev.six-day-war-1967.t: Israel fights Egypt, Syria and Jordan in the Six-Day War of 1967; Egypt and Syria attack in the Yom Kippur War of 1973.
ev.prague-spring-1968.t: The reforms of 1968 are crushed by Warsaw Pact troops in August.
ev.hong-kong-flu-1968.t: The first recorded case was in Hong Kong on 13 July 1968, just after reports of respiratory illness in Guangdong. Singapore, the Philippines, Malaysia and Vietnam had it in August, and India, northern Australia, Europe and the United States in September, the American cases tied to troops home from Vietnam. The USSR followed in December and South America in 1969; Britain’s worst wave came in the winter of 1969–70.
ev.apollo-11.t: Men land on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
ev.arpanet-1969.t: ARPANET and the British NPL network carry the first packet-switched messages in 1969, on the ideas of Donald Davies and Paul Baran.
ev.saigon-1975.t: Saigon falls on 30 April 1975 and the Vietnam War ends.
ev.boat-people.t: Boat departures began in September 1978 and peaked around 1979–1981, to Pulau Bidong, Galang, Hong Kong and the Bataan centre. Of 839,228 Vietnamese who reached UNHCR camps between 1975 and 1997, 749,929 were resettled abroad, 402,382 of them in the United States, 120,403 in France, 108,808 in Australia and 100,012 in Canada; the Orderly Departure Programme of 1979–1994 let others leave by air.
ev.iran-1979.t: The Shah is overthrown; the revolution is complete on 11 February 1979.
ev.afghanistan-1979.t: Soviet forces enter Afghanistan on 24 December 1979.
ev.smallpox-eradicated-1980.t: The World Health Organization declares smallpox eradicated in 1980, 184 years after Jenner’s first vaccination.
ev.mobile-phone-1984.t: Motorola’s DynaTAC 8000X of 1984 is the first mobile phone on the American market. IBM’s Simon of 1994 is the first smartphone.
ev.tiananmen-1989.t: The protests of April–June 1989 end in massacre on 4 June.
ev.revolutions-1989.t: Poland votes on 4 June 1989, the Berlin Wall falls on 9 November, the Velvet Revolution begins in Prague on 24 November and Ceaușescu is executed on 25 December.
ev.www-1990.t: Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first website at CERN on 20 December 1990.
ev.hubble-1990.t: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched in 1990.
ev.ussr-dissolution-1991.n: The dissolution of the Soviet Union
ev.ussr-dissolution-1991.t: The Belovezha Accords dissolve the Union; the Supreme Soviet confirms it on 26 December 1991 and fifteen republics are independent.
ev.yugoslav-wars.t: The Ten-Day War in Slovenia in June 1991 opens the wars; Kosovo ends them in June 1999.
ev.maastricht-1992.t: Signed on 7 February 1992 and in force from 1 November 1993, the treaty creates the European Union.
ev.rwanda-1994.t: The shooting down of the presidents' aircraft on 6 April 1994 triggers the genocide.
ev.mandela-1994.t: Apartheid ends and Nelson Mandela is inaugurated on 10 May 1994.
ev.hong-kong-1997.t: Hong Kong passes from Britain to China on 1 July 1997.
ev.euro-1999.t: The euro is introduced to the markets on 1 January 1999 and enters circulation on 1 January 2002.
ev.nine-eleven.t: About 2,977 people die in the attacks on the United States on 11 September 2001; the invasion of Afghanistan follows on 7 October.
ev.sars-2003.t: The outbreak began in Foshan, Guangdong, on 16 November 2002. In February 2003 an infected guest, Liu Jianlun, stayed at the Metropole Hotel in Hong Kong, and infections seeded there reached Hanoi, Singapore and Toronto by early March. The WHO declared the outbreak contained on 5 July 2003.
ev.iraq-2003.t: The United States invades Iraq on 19 March 2003.
ev.tsunami-2004.t: The earthquake and tsunami of 26 December 2004 kill about 230,000 people.
ev.lehman-2008.t: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008.
ev.h1n1-2009.t: Evidence of the new virus first appeared in February 2009 in La Gloria, Veracruz, where a young boy became known as patient zero, and it reached the United States in April. The WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern on 25 April; air travellers carried the virus to Spain within days and on to Germany, Austria, Britain, Israel and New Zealand. On 10 August 2010 the WHO declared the world in the post-pandemic period.
ev.arab-spring.t: Risings begin in Tunisia in 2010 and spread in 2011 to Egypt, Libya, Yemen, Bahrain and Syria.
ev.fukushima-2011.t: The earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 cause the meltdown at Fukushima.
ev.syrians-2015.t: The flight began with the war in 2011; by 21 December 2015 an estimated 500,000 Syrians had entered Europe, 80% of them by sea into Greece and on through the Balkans, until the route was choked in February 2016. The UNHCR table counts 3,763,565 Syrians in Turkey, 855,172 in Lebanon, 665,404 in Jordan, 562,168 in Germany, 244,760 in Iraq and 131,235 in Egypt.
ev.ebola-2014.t: The index case, a small boy, died at Méliandou in Guinea in December 2013, and the WHO reported the outbreak on 25 March 2014. It reached Liberia’s Lofa and Nimba counties that month and Sierra Leone by May; a traveller carried it to Lagos on 20 July and another to Dallas in September. A nursing assistant in Spain was the first infected outside Africa, and the epidemic was declared over on 9 June 2016.
ev.crimea-2014.t: After Yanukovych's fall in February 2014 Russia annexes Crimea and war begins in the Donbas.
ev.paris-agreement-2015.t: 195 nations agree to cut emissions in December 2015.
ev.crispr-2015.t: The CRISPR method of editing genes is dated to 2015 by the timeline of inventions.
ev.zika-2015.t: Zika broke out on Yap in 2007 and in French Polynesia in 2013, the likely source of the strain that reached Brazil. The Brazilian outbreak was identified in Natal in August 2014, reached Salvador by March 2015 and was confirmed as Zika in May, and a wave of infant microcephaly followed. The WHO declared an emergency on 1 February 2016 and declared the epidemic over in November, after local cases near Miami in August.
ev.brexit-2016.t: Britain votes to leave the European Union on 23 June 2016.
ev.mrna-2020.t: Pfizer and BioNTech’s mRNA vaccine against COVID-19 is approved in 2020, the year of the pandemic.
ev.covid-19.t: The disease was identified in Wuhan in December 2019. The WHO declared an emergency on 30 January 2020 and a pandemic on 11 March, as the virus spread through Iran, Italy, Spain, Brazil and New York, where most infections came from Europe; Delta drove India’s second wave in April 2021 and Omicron was detected in South Africa on 24 November 2021. The emergency ended on 5 May 2023.
ev.ukraine-2022.t: Russia invades Ukraine on 24 February 2022, escalating the war begun in 2014.
ev.ukrainians-2022.t: The UNHCR called it Europe’s fastest-growing refugee crisis since the Second World War: around 7.8 million refugees recorded across Europe by early November 2022, more than 4.5 million of whom had returned by the end of that year. As of May 2025 Germany hosted 1.2 million, Poland about 1 million and the Czech Republic about 0.4 million; 5.3 million were displaced inside Ukraine, and Russia reported 1.2 million Ukrainians in a refugee-like situation in June 2023.
ev.mpox-2022.t: Britain detected the first case in London on 6 May 2022, in a traveller from Nigeria, where the disease is endemic. By 18 May Portugal, Spain, Canada and the United States had cases, Germany confirmed its first on 20 May, and Brazil and Spain recorded the first deaths outside Africa’s endemic countries on 29 July. The WHO declared an emergency on 23 July 2022 and ended it in May 2023.
ev.gaza-2023.t: Hamas attacks Israel on 7 October 2023 and the Gaza war begins.
